items.title: How Slavery Built the Roman Empire
items.description:
Was the Roman Empire really made by conquest? Or was it powered by something much darker? 

For centuries, millions of enslaved people sacrificed their lives and their labour on the altar of Roman progress, an integral cog in the grinding imperial machine. And so today on The Ancients, Tristan Hughes is joined by Dr Emma Southon, author of Servus: How Slavery Made The Roman World to bring their overlooked stories back into the limelight. items.title: The Life of Agis by Plutarch
items.description:
In 245 B.C., Sparta, a once-great Greek city-state, had become corrupt and its citizens had forgotten the laws established by Lycurgus, including rules of dress and inheritance. Traditional Spartan citizens were only allowed to leave their property to their relatives, which had kept the economy stable and the people content. However, the laws were now being ignored, leading to wealth disparity and poverty.

global_silver_linings.title: Two Hours of Sleep Restored in Alzheimer’s Brains in Research Breakthrough
global_silver_linings.snippet: [By Christian Honce | UK College of Medicine] Picture this: You find a small fire isolated in your kitchen. If you had the right tool, you might be able to put it out. But before you can, the sprinklers turn on and soak your entire house.
global_silver_linings.reason: Scientists have found a way to restore two hours of lost sleep in Alzheimer's-affected brains, a meaningful step toward easing one of the disease's most debilitating symptoms. For millions of families living with Alzheimer's, this kind of progress is a genuine reason to keep hoping.

global_silver_linings.title: On a plane, Emilia Clarke imagined she was a butterfly to reach her dying father. Then one was waiting in the house.
global_silver_linings.snippet: "So I knew that he'd passed, and he passed at the time that I was having the dream." The post On a plane, Emilia Clarke imagined she was a butterfly to reach her dying father. Then one was waiting in the house. appeared first on Upworthy .
global_silver_linings.reason: A butterfly waiting at the threshold of grief is a quiet reminder that the natural world can meet us in our most tender moments in ways we can't quite explain. Emilia Clarke's story resonates because it speaks to the comfort many find in nature when words simply aren't enough.
